purpose: Screen the publicly available final report for the Darwin Initiative Cagayan River Basin freshwater project as an alternative, non-government-hosted source route, and distinguish site discovery and project monitoring from reusable species occurrences.

source.title: Sustainable community-based stewardship of freshwater resources in the Northern Philippines: Final Report, project 24-016
source.provider: Zoological Society of London; Darwin Initiative project 24-016, implemented with regional partners
source.reviewedSections: Project summary; freshwater sanctuary table; eel telemetry; invasive-species work; final logframe
source.license: No item-specific open reuse license was identified in the reviewed report.

relatedReviewedSources.relationship: The already-reviewed peer-reviewed article reports the same two-site eel telemetry research and is the stronger primary publication for its methods and sample details. Its reported n=68 differs from the final report's total of 67 acoustically tagged eels; the denominator difference is unresolved.
Earlier project annual report already reviewed for Baggao site labels and illustrative telemetry maps; those maps are not authoritative boundary geometry.

siteDiscoveryQueue.interpretation: These are source-reported freshwater-sanctuary labels useful for prioritizing literature and public-record searches. They are not a complete waterbody inventory, species checklist, verified modern administrative crosswalk, or mapped boundaries. No coordinates or geometry were copied.

reviewedEvidence.eelTelemetry: The final report describes acoustic telemetry arrays at Hot Springs and Duba and says 67 giant mottled eels (Anguilla marmorata) were tagged. The associated 2022 peer-reviewed article is already registered separately and reports n=68. Treat both as historical, site-focused research; do not add a second occurrence series from this project summary.
reviewedEvidence.janitorFishLead: The project summary says research indicated janitor fish were found in the Cagayan River Basin. The report gives no scientific name, sampling event, named waterbody, date, station, voucher, or accession for this statement. It remains an unlocalized source lead, not a species-level occurrence.
reviewedEvidence.invasiveFishSurvey: The final report says an invasive-species survey was carried out in 12 freshwater sanctuaries, that invasive fishes were identified, and that the survey report was prepared and shared with BFAR. It references Annex 32 and Annex 36 in connection with invasive species and fish surveys, but those fish-list data and methods were not included in the publicly reviewed final-report text or located as separate public annex downloads.
reviewedEvidence.stocking: The project reports production of ayungin/freshwater-perch fingerlings and release of 10,000 into the rivers of Tumauini and Cabagan, Isabela. These are managed stocking events, not evidence of a naturally occurring population; exact release dates, stations, taxonomic crosswalk, and post-release observations were not recovered.
reviewedEvidence.siteSpecificity: The report's 12-site table provides municipality, barangay, and sanctuary labels. Except for the separate, already-reviewed eel article, it does not provide a fish species-by-site matrix, sampling-event dates, specimen records, coordinates, or a complete basin checklist.

qualityAndReuseLimits: This is a ZSL-led project report hosted by the Darwin Initiative and produced with regional partners, including government agencies; its accessible hosting is an alternative discovery route, but it does not make the underlying partner survey data openly downloadable.
The generic label 'janitor fish' cannot be resolved to a scientific species from this report and must not be crosswalked to the nearby proposed CSU study label in the separate BFAR annual report.
The invasive-fish survey annex/data were not recovered, so no taxa, site results, methods, event dates, specimen IDs, or coordinates can be extracted from it.
The source describes cultured fish releases; these must remain separate from wild-occurrence and native-range evidence.
No item-specific reuse license was verified. Summaries are research-only; do not reproduce maps, tables, report text, or figures without rights review.
No species/occurrence rows, survey-event rows, stocking records, coordinates, geometry, safety/legal claims, diet claims, or app content are approved from this review.
nextAction: Continue the independent-source path by searching ZSL, Darwin Initiative, university repositories, and the peer-reviewed literature for the project's referenced fish-survey annexes (Annex 32/36) or an equivalent published species-by-site dataset. Prioritize records with exact event locality, dates, scientific identifications, vouchers/accessions, and explicit reuse terms. If those annexes are not public, record the gap and move to other independently accessible Region II waterbody studies; do not make government access the critical path.
